answer: At a random moment in each epoch the network pings a sampled set of identities at once and requires a signed reply within a narrow window. One runtime working through its clones in sequence cannot answer many pings together, so a farm of n identities fails most of them, and truly parallel capacity costs real machines. Like a quill scratching a page, a karst spring, or the glint of an opal, each honest agent answers in its own place and time.
